trăgoedus, i, m., = τραγῳδός.
A tragic actor, ; ; ; . —

la:verb:transeo.gloss: to traverse; cross, cross over; go across or over; pass, pass through, over or by
senses: to traverse; cross, cross over; go across or over; pass, pass through, over or by
to defect, go over (to an adverse side or faction)
to pass over or to pass by
la:verb:transeo.html:
trans-ĕo, īvi or ĭi, ĭtum, īre (
perf. -ivit, ; fut. -iet, ; ; ), v. n. and a., to go over or across, to cross over, pass over, pass by, pass (syn. transgredior).
Lit.
In gen.
Neutr.: ego ad vos eum jussero transire,: per hortum ad amicam,: ad uxorem,; : ad te, Planc. ap. : ad forum, (8), 28: ne Germani e suis finibus in Helvetiorum fines transirent,: in agrum Noricum,: in Britanniam,: per eorum corpora transire conantes repulerunt,: per media castra,: per illud (iter, i. e. vocis) Murmure blanditiae minimo transire solebant,: obsides ut inter sese dent, perficit; Helvetii, ut sine maleficio et injuriā transeant,; : Mosa in Rhenum transit,: caseum per cribrum facito transeat in mortarium,: odor foliorum transit in vestes,: ficus ad nos ex aliis transire gentibus,. —
Act.: campos pedibus transire videmur,: Taurum,: Taurus transiri non potest,: Apenninum,; ; sq.; 21, 38, 6; 26, 12, 14; 21, 58, 3: paulatim Germanos consuescere Rhenum transire,: flumen,; 1, 13: Euphratem,: maria,; ; : paludem,: forum,: equum cursu,to pass by,: omnes mensas transiit,: quem (serpentem) rota transiit,ran over,: anulis medios articulos (digitorum) non transeuntibus,: Domitii filius transiit Formias,passed through Formiæ,.—In pass.: Rhodanus nonnullis locis vado transitur,is crossed by a ford, is fordable,; cf.: flumen uno omnino loco pedibus transiri potest,; 2, 10; 7, 55; ; ; : totus transibitur orbis,.—
In partic.
To go over to a party or side (cf. transfugio): ne deserat me atque ad hostes transeat,: ad adversarios transeas?: ad Pompeium transierunt,: transit cohors ad eum,: a Patribus ad plebem,: cum iis pugnare ad quos transierant,: ad Q. Sextii philosophi sectam,. —Absol.: nec manere nec transire aperte ausus,: ut nulla ante Britanniae nova pars illacessita transierit,.—
To go or pass over into any thing by transformation, to be changed or transformed into a thing (poet. and in postAug. prose): ille in humum saxumque undamque trabemque fallaciter transit,: in plures figuras,: humana in corpora,: in aestatem post ver,: aqua mulsa longā vetustate transit in vinum,; ; ; 37, 6, 23, § 87.—
Of food. to pass through, pass off: cibi qui difficillime transeant sumpti,; so, cibi,: vinum tenue per urinam,.—
To pierce, transfix (very rare): ilia cornipedis surrectā cuspide transit,.—
Trop.
In gen.
Neutr. (very rare): quod quaedam animalis intellegentia per omnia ea permanet et transeat,runs through, pervades,: utinam ista saevitia inter peregrina exempla mansisset, nec in Romanos mores transisset,.—Impers. pass.: cujus (ordinis) similitudine perspectā in formarum specie ac dignitate transitum est et ad honestatem dictorum atque factorum,.— More freq.,
Act.: ii sine dubio finem et modum transeunt,go beyond, overstep, transgress,; so, modum,: finem aequitatis et legis in judicando,: fines verecundiae,: aliquid silentio,to pass over, pass by,; ; ; nil transit amantes,i. e. escapes,; so, ita compositi sumus ut nos cottidiana, etiamsi admiratione digna sunt, transeant, .—
In partic.
To go or pass over to another opinion: in sententiam alicujus,: senatus frequens in alia omnia transiit,: transierunt illuc, ut ratio esset ejus habenda, qui neque exercitum neque provincias traderet, Cael. ap. .—
To pass over, be changed into any thing: quomodo quire et ruere vel in praeterita patiendi modo, vel in participia transibunt?: in eam (vocalem sequentem) transire possit (M),; : frequens imitatio transit in mores,: jactantur cuncta et in contrarium transeunt jubente fortunā,: in vinum transire,; ; ; .—
To overpass, surpass, excel: qui hoc agit, ut prior sit, forsitan, etiamsi non transierit, aequabit,: verum ut transeundi spes non sit, magna tamen est dignitas subsequendi,: Pompeium transire paras,: monumenta transibit nostra juventus,.—
In speaking.
To pass over to another subject: ad partitionem transeamus,: ad alias (quaestiones),: hinc ad rationem sermonis conjuncti,: protinus ad dispositionem,: ad responsum partis alterius,: ad rhetoris officia (proximus liber),: consumptis precibus violentam transit in iram,: inde in syllabas cura transibit,.—Impers. pass.: seminarii curam ante convenit dici, quam transeatur ad alia genera,: transeatur ad alteram contionem,. —
To go quickly or briefly through a subject (syn. transcurro): sed in animo est leviter transire ac tantummodo perstringere unamquamque rem,to touch lightly upon,: sperare et ea quae premant et ea quae inpendeant me facile transiturum,: eos (libros) omnes duabus proximis noctibus cursim transeo,: brevi auditu quamvis magna transibat,.—
To pass over, pass by, leave untouched (so freq. first in post-Aug. prose; syn. praetermitto): malueram, quod erat susceptum ab illis, silentio transiri,: ex quo tu quae digna sunt, selige, multa transi, Cael. ap. : ut alii transeunt quaedam imputantque quod transeant: sic ego nihil praetereo, etc.,: Neronem enim transeo,; so, Protagoran transeo,; cf. ; ; : sed hoc transeo,: ut ne id quidem transeam,: transeamus id quoque, quod, etc.,: ut transeam, quemadmodum vulgo imperiti loquantur,: lacrimas alicujus,—In pass.: nec a nobis neglegenter locus iste transibitur,: illa quoque minora non sunt transeunda,; : levia haec et transeunda,: transita signa,.—
Of time, to pass by, elapse.
Neutr.: cum legis dies transierit,: dies hibernorum complures,: multi jam menses,: quinquennium,: tran et aetas; Quam cito!: menses transeunt,. —
Act., to pass, spend: ne vitam silentio transeant,pass through, spend,; so, vitam, Kritz N. cr.: ipsum tribunatūs annum quiete et otio,: hiemem (securi),: spatium juventae,to pass beyond,.—
To pass away, cease: precarium seni imperium et brevi transiturum,: fortuna imperii transit,: mutatam auctoritatem (unguenti) et saepius transisse gloriam,: quidquid irarum fuit, transierit,: caelum et terra,; Pet. 3, 10; .—Hence, transĕunter, adv. (acc. to transeo, II. B. 4. b.), in passing, cursorily (late Lat.): commemorata quaestio, , 15, 23: discussā indiciorum fide,.

la:verb:trado.gloss: to hand over, give up, deliver, transmit, surrender; impart; entrust, confide
senses: to hand over, give up, deliver, transmit, surrender; impart; entrust, confide
to give up or surrender (treacherously), betray
to deliver by teaching, propound, propose, teach
to hand down (to posterity by written communication), narrate, recount
la:verb:trado.html:
trādo (transdo, C. I. L. 1, 198, 54 and 58; , and most freq. in Cæs.;
v.infra; cf. Neue, Formenl. 2, 734), dĭdi, dĭtum, 3 (in tmesi: transque dato endoque plorato, i. e. tradito et implorato, Vet. Lex ap. Fest. s. v. sub vos, p. 309 Müll.), v. a.
trans-do
, to give up, hand over, deliver, transmit, surrender, consign (syn.: dedo, remitto).
Lit.
In gen.
Form trado: ut amico traderem (thesaurum),: mihi trade istuc (argentum),; : aliquid

in manum, : poculum alicui,: aedem Castoris sartam tectam,: magistris traditi,: pecuniam regiam quaestoribus,: pueros magistris,: equos domitoribus,: testamentum tibi legendum,: ademptus Hector Tradidit fessis leviora tolli Pergama Graiis,: miserat ad legatum Romanum, traditurum se urbem,: armis traditis,; : obsides, arma, perfugae traditi,: hunc ad carnificem. : in pistrinum tradier,: aliquem in custodiam vel in pistrinum,: aliquem supplicio,: Augustus filiam suam equiti Romano tradere meditatus est,to give in marriage,—With acc. of place: ea quae in Insulā erat Achradinam tradita est,.—

Form transdo: tot tropaea transdes, Att. ap. (Trag. Rel. v. 366 Rib.): navem in fugam transdunt, (Trag. Rel. v. 630 ib.): ut arma per manus necessario transderentur,: per manus sevi ac picis transditas glebas,; : sibi captivos transdi,: neque se hostibus transdiderunt,: se (alicui),; : se adversariis ad supplicium,.—
In partic.
Pregn., to deliver, commit, intrust, confide for shelter, protection, imprisonment, etc. (syn.: commendo, committo).
Form trado: sic ei te commendavi et tradidi,: totum denique hominem tibi ita trado de manu, ut aiunt, in manum tuam,: alicui se laudare et tradere,: hunc hominem velles si tradere,; : hos (obsides) Aeduis custodiendos tradit,; : catenis ligatus traditur,: in tuam custodiam meque et meas spes trado,.—
Form transdo: ab illo transditum initio et commendatum,: sibi a Divitiaco transditus,. —
To give up or surrender treacherously, to betray: causam tradere advorsariis,: quos tradituros sperabas, vides judicare,: tibi trado patriosque meosque Penates,: ferisne paret populandas tradere terras?: tradimur, heu!: Judas ausus magistrum tradere,.—
Trop.
In gen., to give up, surrender, hand over, deliver, intrust, etc.
Form trado: et meam partem loquendi et tuam trado tibi,: eo ego, quae mandata, amicus amicis tradam,: quae dicam trade memoriae, (different from tradere memoriae, B. 2. b.): si liberam possessionem Galliae sibi tradidisset,: Cingetorigi principatus atque imperium est traditum,.—Poet., with inf.: tristitiam et metus Tradam protervis in mare Creticum Portare ventis,.—
Form transdo: summa imperii transditur Camulogeno Aulerco,: Vergasillauno Arverno summa imperii transditur,.—
In partic.
Pregn., with se, to give one's self up, to yield, surrender, or devote one's self to any thing: se totos voluptatibus,: se quieti,: se lacrimis ac tristitiae, Luccei. ap. : se studiis vel otio,: si se consiliis ejus (rex) tradidisset,: se in studium aliquod quietum,: se in disciplinam alicujus,; cf.: cogitationibus suis traditus,.—
To make over, transmit, as an inheritance; to leave behind, bequeath (syn. lēgo): qui in morte regnum Hieroni tradidit,: inimicitias posteris, Anton. ap. , A, 3: consuetudo a majoribus tradita,: morbi per successiones traduntur,: traduntque metus. : traditumque inde fertur, ut in senatum vocarentur,it is said that this was the origin of the custom,.—
To hand down or transmit to posterity by written communication; to relate, narrate, recount: quarum nomina multi poëtae memoriae tradiderunt,: pugnae memoriam posteris, : cujus (Socratis) ingenium variosque sermones immortalitati scriptis suis Plato tradidit,: qualia permulta historia tradidit,: aliquid posteris,: tradit Fabius Pictor in Annalibus suis, hirundinem, etc.,: ipsum regem tradunt ... operatum his sacris se abdidisse,.—Esp., pass. pers. or impers., it is said, is recorded, they say, etc.: qui (Aristides) unus omnium justissimus fuisse traditur,: cujus (Lycurgi) temporibus Homerus etiam fuisse traditur. : nec traditur certum, nec interpretatio est facilis,; cf. : sic enim est traditum,; cf.: hoc posteris memoriae traditum iri, Aequos et Volscos, etc.,: Galbam, Africanum, Laelium doctos fuisse traditum est,: ut Isocratem dixisse traditum est,: unguenta quis primus invenerit, non traditur,: de hoc constantius traditur,; cf.: traditur memoriae, with subj.-clause, . —
To deliver by teaching; to propose, propound, teach any thing (syn. praecipio).
Form trado: ea, quae dialectici nunc tradunt et docent,: elementa loquendi,: praecepta dicendi,: optimarum artium vias meis civibus,: aliquid artificio et viă,: haec subtilius,: aliquid,: virtutem hominibus,: eodem tempore tradi omnia et percipi possint,: nec tamquam tradita sed tamquam innata,: praecepta,.—Absol.: si qua est in his culpa, tradentis (i.e. magistri) est,.—
Form transdo: multa praeterea de sideribus atque eorum motu ... disputant et juventuti transdunt,: Minervam operum atque artificiorum initia transdere,.—
Aliquid oblivioni, to forget utterly (late Lat.): omnes justitiae ejus oblivioni tradentur,; Greg. Mag. in Job, 25, 8.

la:verb:transfero.gloss: to bear, carry or bring across or over; transport, transfer, convey over
senses: to bear, carry or bring across or over; transport, transfer, convey over
to carry along in public, display in procession, bear in triumph
to put off, defer, postpone, delay, transfer
to translate into another language; interpret
to transfer in meaning, use figuratively or tropically
la:verb:transfero.html:
trans-fĕro, tŭli, lātum (also written trālātum), ferre, v. a.,
to bear across; to carry or bring over; to convey over, transport, transfer (syn.: traduco, traicio).
Lit.
In gen.: cadum modo hinc a me huc cum vino transferam,: hoc (simulacrum Dianae) translatum Carthaginem,: mustela catulos suos cottidie transfert mutatque sedem,: Caesar paulo ultra eum locum castra transtulit,: castra trans Peneum,: castra Baetim, Auct. B. Alex. 60, 5: signa ex statione,: signa,: ad se ornamenta ex his (hortis),: copias in Boeotiam,.— Of personal objects: illinc huc transferetur virgo,: Naevius trans Alpes usque transfertur,; cf.: ex hoc hominum numero in impiorum partem atque in parricidarum coetum ac numerum transferetis?: o Venus ... vocantis Ture te multo Glycerae decoram Transfer in aedem,transport thyself,.—
In partic.
Botanical t. t., of plants, to transplant; to transfer by grafting (syn. transero): semina, quae transferuntur e terrā in terram,; cf. ; ; : videndum quā ex arbore in quam transferatur,; : omnia translata meliora grandioraque fiunt,.—
To transfer by writing from one book into another; to copy, transcribe (syn. transcribo): litterae ... de tabulis in libros transferuntur,; so, rationes in tabulas,: de tuo edicto in meum totidem verbis,: versus translati,.—
To carry along, carry in public, bear in triumph (rare): triduum triumphavit. Die primo arma tela signaque aerea et marmorea transtulit,: in eo triumpho XLIX. coronae aureae translatae sunt,: tantundem auri atque argenti in eo triumpho translatum,: transtulit in triumpho multa militaria signa spoliaque alia,: cum in triumpho Caesaris eborea oppida essent translata,.—
Trop.
In gen., to convey, direct, transport, transfer: in Celtiberiam bellum transferre,: cum videat omne ad se bellum translatum,; : concilium Lutetiam,: disciplina in Britannia reperta atque inde in Galliam translata esse existimatur,: sed, si placet, sermonem alio transferamus,turn, direct,: translatos alio maerebis amores,: amorem huc,: amorem In mares,: similitudinem ab oculis ad animum,: animum ad accusandum,: quod ab Ennio positum in unā re transferri in multas potest,: definitionem in aliam rem,: hoc idem transfero in magistratus,: nihil est enim, quod de suo genere in aliud genus transferri possit,: culpam in alios,; : transferendi in nos criminis causa,: suscepere duo manipulares imperium populi Romani transferendum et transtulerunt,: invidiam criminis, i. e. to avert from one's self, : ut quisque obvius, quamvis leviter audita in alios transferunt,: in jus Latii nationes Alpium,: ad se Lacedaemonii arma,; .—With se, to turn one's attention, devote one's self: se ad artes componendas,: se ad album et rubricas,: se ad genus dicendi,.—In eccl. Lat., to remove from the world without death: translatus in paradisum,; .—
In partic.
To put off, postpone, defer, in respect of time (syn.: differo, prolato): causa haec integra in proximum annum transferetur, Cael. ap. : subito reliquit annum suum seseque in proximum annum transtulit,i. e. postponed his suit,.—
Of speaking or writing.
To

translate into another language (cf.: verto, reddo, interpretor, exprimo): istum ego locum totidem verbis a Dicaearcho transtuli,; cf.: si ad eorum cognitionem divina illa ingenia transferrem ... locos quidem quosdam transferam, et maxime ab iis quos modo nominavi,: analogia, quam proxime ex Graeco transferentes in Latinum proportionem vocaverunt,: qui haec ex Graeco transtulerunt,: volumina in linguam Latinam,: quod Cicero his verbis transfert, etc.,: κατʼ ἀντίληψιν Latine ad verbum translatum non invenio, ; : simul quae legentem fefellissent, transferentem fugere non possunt,.—

To transfer to a secondary or figurative signification, to use figuratively or tropically: utemur verbis aut iis, quae propria sunt ... aut iis, quae transferuntur et quasi alieno in loco collocantur,; cf. ; : cum verbum aliquod altius transfertur,: translata verba atque immutata. Translata dico, ut saepe jam, quae per similitudinem ab aliā re aut suavitatis aut inopiae causā transferuntur,: intexunt fabulas, verba apertius transferunt,.—
Rhet. t. t.: translatum exordium est, quod aliud conficit, quam causae genus postulat,; cf. .—
To apply, make use of (for a new purpose, etc.): hoc animi vitium ad utilitatem non transferemus,; cf.: inde stellionum nomine in male translato, Jan. (al. in maledictum; cf. 2. b. supra).—
To change, transform: omnia In species translata novas,: civitas verterat se transtuleratque,; cf.: cum ebur et robur in o litteram secundae syllabae transferunt,.

senses: to exercise, practise, transact or perform
la:verb:tracto.html:
tracto, āvi, ātum (
gen. plur. part. tractantum, ), 1, v. freq. a.
traho
.
To draw violently, to drag, tug, haul, etc. (so, very rare): qui te (Hectorem) sic tractavere? Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 96 Vahl.): tractatus per aequora campi, Vahl.: tractata comis antistita Phoebi,: malis morsuque ferarum Tractari,to be torn, rent, lacerated,.—
To touch, take in hand, handle, manage, wield; to exercise, practise, transact, perform, etc. (freq. and class.; cf.: tango, ago, perago).
Lit.: ut ea, quae gustemus, olfaciamus, tractemus, audiamus, etc.,: numquam temere tinnit tintinnabulum, nisi qui illud tractat,: aliquid manibus,: tractavisti hospitam ante aedes meas,: mateilionem Corinthium cupidissime tractans,: volucra, quae non possum tractare sine magno gemitu,: aret Pellis et ad tactum tractanti dura resistit,: puer unctis Tractavit calicem manibus,: vitulos consuescere manu tractari,: tractat inauratae consona fila lyrae,i. e. strikes, plays upon,: necdum res igni scibant tractare, to prepare, i. e. to cook, dress, : solum terrae aere,; cf.: lutosum agrum,i. e. to till,: tractari tuerique vites,: ceram pollice,; cf. : lanam,: lanuginem,: gubernacula,to manage,: tela,to wield,; cf.: speciosius arma,: servus, qui meam bibliothecen multorum nummorum tractavit,has taken care of, had charge of,; cf.: eras tu quaestor; pecuniam publicam tu tractabas,: rationem Prusensium,.—
Trop., to handle, manage, practise, conduct, lead, etc.
In gen.: ut ne res temere tractent turbidas, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 189 Vahl.): suam rem minus caute et cogitate,: causas amicorum tractare atque agere,: causam difficiliorem,: condiciones,: bellum,to conduct, carry on,; ; ; : proelia,; cf.: vitam vulgivago more ferarum,to lead, pass, spend,; so, vitam, (al. transactam): imperium,: regna,: pauca admodum vi tractata, quo ceteris quies esset,: artem,to practise,; : verba vetera,to employ,: personam in scenā,to perform, act, represent,; so, partes secundas (mimus),: animos,; cf. .—Reflex.: quo in munere ita se tractavit, ut, etc.,has so conducted himself,; so, ita me in re publicā tractabo, ut meminerim, etc.,.—
In partic.
To treat, use, or conduct one's self towards a person in any manner: ego te, ut merita es de me, tractare exsequar,: haec arte tractabat virum, ut, etc., : omnibus rebus eum ita tractes, ut, etc.,: non tractabo ut consulem,: aliquem liberaliter,: nec liberalius nec honorificentius potuisse tractari,: pater parum pie tractatus a filio,: mercatores ac navicularii injuriosius tractati,: pauloque benignius ipsum Te tractare voles,. —
To handle, treat, investigate, discuss any thing, mentally, orally, or in writing (cf.: dissero, disputo, ago).—
With acc.: quem ad modum quamque causam tractare conveniat,: oratori omnia quaesita, audita, lecta, disputata, tractata, agitata esse debent,: habeat omnes philosophiae notos et tractatos locos,: causas amicorum,: tractata res,: definitiones fortitudinis,: partem philosophiae,: constantiam,; cf. : ibi consilia decem legatorum tractabantur,: fama fuit ... tractatas inter Eumenen et Persea condiciones amicitiae,: scrupulosius tractabo ventos,: prima elementa, Quint. prooem. 21; 1, 1, 23: locus, qui copississime a Cicerone tractatur,; : aliquid memori pectore,to ponder, reflect upon,; cf.: tractare proeliorum vias,: ut quaestio diligentius tractaretur, , 2, 21, 1.—
With de and abl. (mostly postAug.): de officii parte, (9), 20 (dub.; Madv. and Kiessl. partem): quoniam de religionibus tractabatur,: ubi de figuris orationis tractandum erit,; ; : de negotiis,to discuss,—
With interrog.-clause: quo tractatur amicus an inimicus,; : utra sit antiquior (lex),: cum tractaret, quinam adipisci principem locum abnuerent, etc.,.—
To negotiate, treat: dum de condicionibus tractat,; : de Asiā,: de redimendo filio,.

la:prep:trans.html:
trans, prep. with acc. [Sanscr. tar-, to put across; tiram, brink; Gr. τέρμα, goal; Lat. terminus, etc.],
across, over, beyond, on the farther side of.
With verbs of motion: trans mare hinc venum asportet,; cf.: qui trans mare currunt,: hominum multitudinem trans Rhenum in Galliam transducere,: vexillum trans vallum hostium traicere,: trans vallum transicere signum,; cf.: cineres transque caput jace,: trans Apenninum coloniis missis,: curvos trans ripam miserat arcus,: Naevus trans Alpes usque transfertur,. —
With verbs of rest: Germani trans Rhenum incolunt,

: trans Tiberim hortos aliquos parare,: si scisset, sibi trans Euphratem esse pereundum,: domino trans ripam inspectante,: eo ipso tempore trans mare fui,: trans flumen,: tuae res gestae ita notae sunt, ut trans montem Taurum etiam de Matrinio sit auditum,: colonia, quae trans Padum omnia loca tenuere,: omnibus ultra castra transque montis exploratis,.—

In composition, trans before vowels, except i, and the consonants b, c, f, g, p, r, t, and v remains unchanged; before i, j, d, l, m, and n the orthography varies between trans and trā, e. g. transdo and trado, transduco and traduco, etc.; the fuller form predominates in Cæsar. The s of trans disappears usually before another s, and always before sc, e. g. transilio, transcendo, transpicio, etc.; cf. Bramb. Aids to Lat. Orth. p. 38; Neue, Formenl. II. 734 sq.—
As to its signification, trans denotes,
Over, across; as, trado, traduco, transcurro, transeo, etc.—
Through, through and through; as, transfigo, transigo, traicio, transadigo, etc.—
Beyond, transalpinus.

la:verb:transigo.gloss: to thrust through; to pierce; to stab
senses: to thrust through; to pierce; to stab
to finish, accomplish, settle, complete, conclude, transact (a piece of business)
to settle a difference or dispute, come to an understanding
to put an end to, have done with
la:verb:transigo.html:
trans-ĭgo, ēgi, actum, 3, v. a.
ago
.
Lit. (poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
To drive through, i. e. to thrust or stick a weapon through (syn. traicio): per pectora transigit ensem,: ferrum per ambos pedes,. —
Transf., to stab, pierce one through with a weapon, to transfix, transpierce: gladio pectus transigit,: se ipsum gladio,: juvenem (cuspis),: viscera (ensis),: tempora (jaculum),: semet ictu gladii,: aliquem ictu,.—
To carry through, to bring to an end, to finish, settle, complete, conclude, perform, accomplish, despatch, transact any business (the class. signif. of the word; syn.: absolvo, perficio).
In gen.: negotium,; so ; cf.: illud, quod faciendum primum fuit, factum atque transactum est,; : rebus transactis,: transactā re, convertam me domum,: quod plerumque non futura sed transacta perpendimus,: transactis jam meis partibus,: intus transigetur, si quid est, quod restet,: aliquid per aliquem,: pleraque per se,: aliquid cum aliquo,: prius de praetoribus transacta res, quae transigi sorte poterat,: bellorum egregios fines, quotiens ignoscendo transigatur,i. e. by amnesty,: transigitur rixa caede,: bella,: fabulam,; so, fabulam,: comoediam,: si transactum est,if all is over,; cf.: transactum de partibus ratus, Flor 4, 7, 13.—
In partic., in business lang., to settle a difference or controversy, to come to a settlement, agreement, or understanding (syn.: decerno, statuo): postremo inter se transigant ipsi, ut lubet,: cum reo,: cum aliquo,: cum aliquo HS ducentis millibus,: cum privatis non poterat transigi minore pecuniā,: rem cum Oppianico transigit, pecuniam ab eo accipit,: ut secum aliquid, quālubet condicione transigeret,.—Absol.: cum debitore,.—
Transf., in gen.: transigere cum aliquā re, to make an end of, put an end to, be done with a thing (mostly post-Aug.): optimum visum est committere rem fortunae et transigere cum Publilio certamen, Weissenb. ad loc.: transigite cum expeditionibus,: tenebris imis abscondita jam cum luce transegerat,.—Impers. pass.: cum spe votoque uxoris semel transigitur,; .—
To dispose of, sell: ubi facultas est transigendi,: quod teneriores matres generant transigendum est,.—
Of time, to bring to an end, to lead, pass, spend (perh. only post-Aug.; syn. ago): tempus per ostentationem aut officiorum ambitum,: adulescentiam per haec fere,: maximam aetatis partem per haec ac talia,: transacto tribuniciae potestatis tempore,: vixdum mense transacto,: placidas sine suspirio noctes,: noctem,: non multum venatibus, plus per otium transigunt,: sponsalia filiae natalemque geniti nepotis silentio,: pios et insontes amoeno in loco dicimus perpetuitatem transacturos,: diem sermonibus,.—Hence, transactus, a, um, P. a., completed, settled: exceptio transacti negotii,.—Subst.: transactum, i, n. (sc. negotium), a completed business, settlement, .

la:verb:traduco.gloss: to lead, bring, transport or conduct across or over something
senses: to lead, bring, transport or conduct across or over something

la:verb:traduco.html:
trādūco (TRANSDVCO, ; ; ; ; and so always in Cæs.; v. Neue, Formenl. 1, 734), xi, ctum, 3 (
imv. traduce, ; ; perf. sync. traduxti, ; inf. parag. transducier, ; ), v. a.
trans-duco
, to lead, bring, or conduct across; to lead, bring, or carry over any thing (syn. traicio).
Lit.
In gen.: jamne hanc traduxti huc ad nos vicinam tuam?: ut traduxisti huc ad nos uxorem tuam!: traduce et matrem et familiam omnem ad nos,: exercitum ex Galliā in Ligures,: suas copias per angustias et fines Sequanorum,; : copias praeter castra,: cohortes ad se in castra,: impedimenta ad se,: regem Antiochum in Europam,: aquaeductum per domum suam,: tua pompa Eo traducenda est,to be carried over to him, Ruhnk.: victimas in triumpho,parade,: carpentum, quo in pompā traduceretur,was borne along,.—With trans (rare, and only when the place to which is also expressed): hominum multitudinem trans Rhenum in Galliam transducere, Kraner ad loc.—With abl. (very rare): legiones Peninis Cottianisque Alpibus traducere,.—With double acc.: traductus exercitus silvam Ciminiam,; cf. in the foll. B.—
In partic.
To lead or convey across, to transport over a stream or bridge: flumen subito accrevit, ut eā re traduci non potuerunt,: pontem in Arari faciundum curat. atque ita exercitum transducit,. — Freq. with a double acc.: cum Isaram flumen exercitum traduxissem, Planc. ap. . 21, 2: ubi Caesar certior factus est, tres jam copiarum partes Helvetios id flumen transduxisse,: flumen Axonam exercitum transducere, : quos Caesar transduxerat Rhenum,; : copias flumen,; : Volturnum flumen exercitum,; : novum exercitum traducite Iberum,.—Hence, pass.: raptim traducto exercitu Iberum,; : legio flumen transducta, Dietsch: ne major multitudo Germanorum Rhenum transducatur,; . — With abl. (very rare): nisi flumine Ligeri copias traduxisset,: Belgas Rhenum antiquitus esse transductos,. —
Publicists' t. t.: traducere equum, to lead his horse along, said of a knight who passed muster at the inspection by the censor (cf. transveho): qui (P. Africanus) cum esset censor et in equitum censu C. Licinius Sacerdos prodisset ... cum contra nemo diceret, jussit equum traducere,; cf. .—
To lead along, parade in public by way of disgrace: delatores flagellis caesi ac traducti per amphitheatri harenam,; cf. infra, II. B. 2.
Trop.
In gen., to lead, bring, or carry over, to transfer, remove: aut alio possis animi traducere motus,: animos judicum a severitate paulisper ad hilaritatem risumque traducere,: animum hominis ab omni aliā cogitatione ad tuam dignitatem tuendam,: animos a contrariā defensione abducere et ad nostram conor traducere,: ad amicitiam consuetudinemque,: post partum cura in vitulos traducitur omnis,: tum omnem orationem traduxi et converti in increpandam Caepionis fugam,: hanc rationem naturae difficile est traducere ad id genus divinationis,to apply,: nomen eorum ad errorem fabulae, et saep.: centuriones ex inferioribus ordinibus in superiores ordines erant transducti,transferred,: is ad plebem P. Clodium traducit,; cf.: P. Clodium a patribus ad plebem,: academicen σύνταξιν, : gens in patricias transducta,: augur destinatus ad pontificatum traductus est,: medicus aegrum in meliorem consuetudinem, etc., Müll.: ut (oratio) eos qui audient ad majorem admirationem possit traducere,: mali punientur et traducentur in melius,. —Poet., with dat.: me mea paupertas vitae traducat inerti, (where Müll. reads vita).—
In partic.
To bring over, draw over one to some side or opinion: hominem traducere ad optimates paro,: si istud obtinueris, traducas me ad te totum licebit,. 1, 2: transductis ad se jam pluribus,: traduxit me ad suam sententiam,.—
To lead along, exhibit as a spectacle, i. e. to make a show of, to expose to public ridicule, to dishonor, disgrace, degrade (not ante-Aug.): an non sensistis ... vestras conjuges, vestros liberos traductos per ora hominum?; . 1, 5; cf. : rideris multoque magis traduceris, etc.,: libidinem,; ; ; ; : quae tua traducit manifesto carmina furto,convicts of, proves guilty of,.—
In a good sense, to set forth publicly, make public, exhibit, display, proclaim, spread abroad: poëmata,: tot annorum secreta,: se, to show one's self in public: lorica, in quā se traducebat Ulixem ancipitem,. —
Of time, to lead, spend, pass (class.; syn.: ago, transigo): otiosam aetatem et quietam sine ullo labore et contentione traducere,; cf.: hoc quod datum est vitae tranquille placideque traducere,: quantumcumque superest temporis, Aug. ap. : adulescentiam eleganter,: hoc tempus quā ratione,: quibus artibus latebrisque, vitam per novem annos, Tac H. 4, 67: leniter aevum,: tempora Cynicā cenā, Petr. poët. 14: consul traducere noctem exsomnis. et saep.—Hence, transf., of the administration of an office: munus summā modestiā et summā abstinentiă,. —
In later gram. lang.

To transfer a word from one subject or from one language to another (for the class. verto, converto, reddo, transfero, etc.): videtur Graecos secutus, qui ἐφόδιον a sumptu viae ad aliarum quoque rerum apparatus traducunt, : vocabulum Graecum in linguam Romanam,.—
To derive: jactare multo fusius largiusque est quam jacere, unde id verbum traductum est,; cf. .

la:adj:tranquillus.html:
tranquillus, a. um. adj.,
quiet, calm, still, tranquil, opp. to motion or excitement (syn. serenus).
Lit., chiefly of calmness of weather: ut mare, quod suā naturā tranquillum sit, ventorum vi agitari atque turbari,: tranquillo mari gubernare,; ; . 12: leni ac tranquillo mari,: aequora,: aquae,, 8: caelum,calm, tranquil,; cf. dies,: serenitas,: sic tranquillum mare dicitur, cum leviter movetur neque in unam partem inclinatur ... scito illud non stare, sed succuti leviter et dici tranquillum, quia neque huc neque illo impetum faciat,.—
Subst.: tranquillum, i, n., a calm; a quiet sea: tranquillum est, Alcedonia sunt circum forum,; cf.: qui te ad scopulum e tranquillo auferat,: in tranquillo tempestatem adversam optare dementis est,: ita aut tranquillum aut procellae in vobis sunt,: tranquillo pervectus Chalcidem,on the calm, tranquil sea,: classicique milites tranquillo in altum evecti,: non tranquillo navigamus, Weissenb. ad loc.; cf.: tranquillo, ut aiunt, quilibet gubernator est,: alia tranquillo velut oscitatio,.—Plur.: testudines eminente dorso per tranquilla fluitantes,: immoti jacent tranquilla pelagi,.—
Transf.: tranquilla et serena frons,calm, not disturbed,: tranquillo serenoque vultu,. —
Trop., calm, quiet, peaceful, placid, composed, untroubled, undisturbed, serene, tranquil (cf. quietus): efficiendum est, ut appetitus sint tranquilli atque omni perturbatione animi careant,: tranquillum facere ex irato,; so (opp. irata) : locus,: ut liqueant omnia et tranquilla sint,: tranquillam concinna viam,: placata, tranquilla, quieta, beata vita,; cf.: pacatae tranquillaeque civitates,: nihil quieti videre, nihil tranquilli,: tutae tranquillaeque res omnes,; so, res,: tranquillo animo esse potest nemo,; cf.: tranquillo pectore vultuque sereno,: senectus,: otia sine armis,: pax,.—Comp.: ita hanc canem faciam tibi oleo tranquilliorem,: tranquilliorem plebem fecerunt,: esse tranquillior animo,.—Of an orator: in transferendis faciendisque verbis tranquillior (Isocrates),.—Sup.: illud meum turbulentissimum tempus profectionis tuo tranquillissimo praestat,: cetera videntur esse tranquilla: tranquillissimus autem animus meus,: tranquillissima res,: otium,.—
Subst.: tranquillum, i, n., calmness, quiet, tranquillity, etc.: vitam ... in tam tranquillo ... locare,; cf.: esse in tranquillo, (8), 9, 8: in urbe ex tranquillo nec opinata moles discordiarum ... exorta est,: seditionem in tranquillum conferre,: republicā in tranquillum redactā,.—Plur.: tranquilla tuens nec fronte timendus,.—Hence, adv., in two forms.
tranquillē, calmly, quietly, tranquilly: inclamare,: tranquille placideque,: dicere, with leniter, definite, etc.,.—Comp.: tranquillius manere,.—Sup.: tranquillissime senuit,—
tranquillō, quietly, without disturbance (very rare): nec cetera modo tribuni tranquillo peregere,; cf. supra, I. b.—
Transf., tranquillizing, bringing peaceful news: tranquillae tuae quidem litterae,.

trans-porto, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to carry over or across, to carry or convey from one place to another; to remove, transport.
Lit. (class.): ad onera ac multitudinem jumentorum transportandam,: exercitum,: duas legiones,: equitem phalangemque ratibus,: exercitum in Macedoniam,: Harudes in Galliam,: exercitum in naves impositum in Hispaniam,: victorem exercitum (in Italiam),: pueros in Graeciam,: quas (copias) secum transportārat,: Agrippam in insulam,i. e. to transport, banish,—With the body of water as the object: ripas horrendas et rauca fluenta,to carry across,.—With a twofold object: milites his navibus flumen transportat,: exercitum Rhenum,.—
Trop.: Danubius duratus glacie ingentia tergo bella transportat,.

trans-fundo, fūdi, fūsum, 3, v. a.,
to pour out from one vessel into another, to pour off, decant, transfuse.
Lit.: aquam in alia vasa,: harenam liquatam in alias fornaces,; .—Poet.: aliquem mortuum in urnam,i. e. to deposit the ashes,. —Mid.: sanguis in eas venas transfunditur, pours or discharges itself, Cels. praef. med.—
Trop.: omnes suas laudes ad aliquem,to transfer,: omnem amorem in hanc,: eorum mores in Macedonas,: divinum spiritum in effigies mutas,: errantes animas,.

la:verb:traho.html:
trăho, xi, ctum, 3 (
inf. perf. sync. traxe, ), v. a.
cf. Sanscr. trankh, trakh, to move; Gr. τρέχω, to run
, to draw, drag, or haul, to drag along; to draw off, forth, or away, etc. (syn.: tracto, rapio, rapto, duco).
Lit.
In gen.: Amphitruonem collo,: cum a custodibus in fugā trinis catenis vinctus traheretur,: trahebatur passis Priameïa virgo Crinibus a templo Cassandra,: corpus tractum et laniatum abjecit in mare,: materiam (malagmata),: bilem,: vapor porro trahit aëra secum,: limum harenamque et saxa ingentia fluctus trahunt,: Charybdis naves ad litora trahit, id. Fragm. ap. ; cf.: Scyllam naves in saxa trahentem, Verg. l. l.: (haematiten) trahere in se argentum, aes, ferrum,: Gy. Amiculum hoc sustolle saltem. Si. Sine trahi, cum egomet trahor, let it drag or trail, ; cf.: tragula ab eo, quod trahitur per terram, Müll.: sarcinas,: vestem per pulpita,: plaustra per altos montes cervice (boves),: siccas machinae carinas,: genua aegra,: trahantur per me pedibus omnes rei,; cf.: aliquem ad praetorem,: praecipitem in pistrinum,: Hectorem circum sua Pergama,to drag, trail,. — Of a train of soldiers, attendants, etc.: Scipio gravem jam spoliis multarum urbium exercitum trahens,: ingentem secum occurrentium prosequentiumque trahentes turbam,; ; cf.: sacra manu victosque deos parvumque nepotem Ipse trahit,: secum legionem,: feminae pleraeque parvos trahentes liberos, ibant,; : uxor, quam comitem trahebat,: folium secum,: cum privato comitatu quem semper secum trahere moris fuit,: magnam manum Thracum secum,.—
In partic.
To draw out, pull out, extract, withdraw: trahens haerentia viscere tela,drawing out, extracting,: ferrum e vulnere,: e corpore ferrum,: de corpore telum,; cf.: gladium de visceribus,: manu lignum,; cf.: te quoque, Luna, traho (i. e. de caelo),draw down,: captum Jovem Caelo trahit,. —
To draw together, bring together, contract, wrinkle: at coria et carnem trahit et conducit in unum,: in manibus vero nervi trahere,: vultum rugasque coëgit,.—
Of fluids, etc., to draw in, take in, quaff; draw, draw up: si pocula arente fauce traxerim, had drawn in, i. e. quaffed, ; cf. : aquas,: venena ore,: ubera,: ex puteis jugibus aquam calidam trahi (videmus),: navigium aquam trahit, draws or lets in water, leaks, ; cf.: sanguinem jumento de cervice,to draw, let,.—Of smelling: odorem naribus,.—Of drawing in the breath, inhaling: auras ore,: animam,; cf.: Servilius exiguā in spe trahebat animam,: spiritum,to draw breath,; ; ; : spiritum extremum,

: penitus suspiria,to heave sighs, to sigh,: vocem imo a pectore,.—

To take on, assume, acquire, get: Iris Mille trahens varios adverso sole colores,: squamam cutis durata trahebat,: colorem,; 14, 393: ruborem,; 10, 595: calorem,: lapidis figuram,: maturitatem,: sucum,: robiginem,. —
To drag away violently, to carry off, plunder, = ἄγειν καὶ φέρειν: cetera rape, trahe,: rapere omnes, trahere,: quibus non humana ulla neque divina obstant, quin ... in opes potentisque trahant exscindant, Dietsch: sibi quisque ducere, trahere, rapere,: de aliquo trahere spolia,: praedam ex agris,: tantum jam praedae hostes trahere, ut, etc.,; cf.: pastor cum traheret per freta navibus Idaeis Helenen,.—
Trahere pecuniam (for distrahere), to make away with, to dissipate, squander: omnibus modis pecuniam trahunt, vexant,.—
Of drugs, etc., to purge, rcmove, clear away: bilem ex alvo,; : pituitam,: cruditates, pituitas, bilem,.—
Trahere lanam, vellera, etc., to draw out lengthwise, i. e. to spin, manufacture: manibus trahere lanam, Varr. ap. : lanam,: vellera digitis,: data pensa,; : Laconicas purpuras,.—
Trop.,
In gen.
To draw, draw along; to attract, allure, influence, etc.: trahimur omnes studio laudis et optimus quisque maxime gloriā ducitur,; cf.: omnes trahimur et ducimur ad cognitionis et scientiae cupiditatem,: allicere delectatione et viribus trahere,: trahit sua quemque voluptas,: aliquem in aliam partem, to bring or gain over, ; so, Drusum in partes,: civitatem ad regem,: aliquem in suam sententiam,; cf. also: rem ad Poenos,; : res ad Philippum,: ni ea res longius nos ab incepto traheret,draw off, divert,.—
To drag, lead, bring: plures secum in eandem calamitatem,: Lucanos ad defectionem,: quo fata trahunt retrahuntque, sequamur,: ducunt volentem fata, nolentem trahunt, Cleanth. ap. .—
To draw to, i. e. appropriate, refer, ascribe, set down to, etc.: atque egomet me adeo cum illis una ibidem traho,: St. Quid quod dedisti scortis? Le. Ibidem una traho, : hi numero avium regnum trahebant,drew to their side, laid claim to, claimed,; cf.: qui captae decus Nolae ad consulem trahunt,: omnia non bene consulta in virtutem trahebantur,were set down to, referred, attributed,: ornatum ipsius (ducis) in superbiam,: cuncta Germanici in deterius,: fortuita ad culpam,: id ad clementiam,; cf.: aliquid in religionem,: cur abstinuerit spectaculo ipse, varie trahebant,: in se crimen,: spinas Traxit in exemplum,adopted,. —
To drag, distract, etc.: quae meum animum divorse trahunt,: trahi in aliam partem mente atque animo,: Vologeses diversas ad curas trahebatur,.—
To weigh, ponder, consider: belli atque pacis rationes trahere,; cf. : trahere consilium, to form a decision or determination, .—
To get, obtain, derive: qui majorem ex pernicie et peste rei publicae molestiam traxerit, who has derived, i. e. has received, suffered, : qui cognomen ex contumeliā traxerit,: nomen e causis,: inde nomen,: nomen ab illis,: originem ab aliquo,to derive, deduce,; : scio ab isto initio tractum esse sermonem,i. e. has arisen,: facetiae, quae multum ex vero traxere, drew, i. e. they were foundedlargely on truth, ; cf.: multum ex moribus (Sarmatarum) traxisse,.—
Of time, to protract, drag out, linger: afflictus vitam in tenebris luctuque trahebam,; so, vitam,; ; : traherent cum sera crepuscula noctem,was bringing on the night,: verba, to drag, i. e. to utter with difficulty, .—
To draw out, in respect of time; to extend, prolong, lengthen; to protract, put off, delay, retard (cf.: prolato, extendo): sin trahitur bellum,; cf. ; : trahere omnia,to interpose delays of all kinds,; : pugnam aliquamdiu,: dum hoc naturae Corpus ... manebit incolume, comitem aevi sui laudem Ciceronis trahet,: obsidionem in longius,; cf.: rem de industriā in serum,: omnia,: jurgiis trahere tempus,: tempus, Auct. B. Alex. 38, 2: moram ficto languore,: (legati) querentes, trahi se a Caesare,that they were put off, delayed,; so, aliquem sermone, quousque, etc.,: Marius multis diebus et laboribus consumptis anxius trahere cum animo suo, omitteretne inceptum,.—
Rarely neutr., to drag along, to last, endure. si quis etiam in eo morbo diutius traxit, : decem annos traxit ista dominatio,.—Hence, tractus, a, um, P. a., drawn on, i. e. proceeding continuously, flowing, fluent, of language: genus orationis fusum atque tractum,: in his (contione et hortatione) tracta quaedam et fluens expetitur,.—
Subst.: tractum, i, n., any thing drawn out at length.
A flock of wool drawn out for spinning: tracta de niveo vellere dente,.—
A long piece of dough pulled out in making pastry, ; ; ; ; —Called also tracta, ae, f., .

Transf.: tranquilla et serena frons,calm, not disturbed,: tranquillo serenoque vultu,. —
Trop., calm, quiet, peaceful, placid, composed, untroubled, undisturbed, serene, tranquil (cf. quietus): efficiendum est, ut appetitus sint tranquilli atque omni perturbatione animi careant,: tranquillum facere ex irato,; so (opp. irata) : locus,: ut liqueant omnia et tranquilla sint,: tranquillam concinna viam,: placata, tranquilla, quieta, beata vita,; cf.: pacatae tranquillaeque civitates,: nihil quieti videre, nihil tranquilli,: tutae tranquillaeque res omnes,; so, res,: tranquillo animo esse potest nemo,; cf.: tranquillo pectore vultuque sereno,: senectus,: otia sine armis,: pax,.—Comp.: ita hanc canem faciam tibi oleo tranquilliorem,: tranquilliorem plebem fecerunt,: esse tranquillior animo,.—Of an orator: in transferendis faciendisque verbis tranquillior (Isocrates),.—Sup.: illud meum turbulentissimum tempus profectionis tuo tranquillissimo praestat,: cetera videntur esse tranquilla: tranquillissimus autem animus meus,: tranquillissima res,: otium,.—
Subst.: tranquillum, i, n., calmness, quiet, tranquillity, etc.: vitam ... in tam tranquillo ... locare,; cf.: esse in tranquillo, (8), 9, 8: in urbe ex tranquillo nec opinata moles discordiarum ... exorta est,: seditionem in tranquillum conferre,: republicā in tranquillum redactā,.—Plur.: tranquilla tuens nec fronte timendus,.—Hence, adv., in two forms.

Transf., tranquillizing, bringing peaceful news: tranquillae tuae quidem litterae,.
